newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TVNZ swaps regional services for new youth channel.
newsitem.headline: TVNZ swaps regional services for new youth channel.

text.p: Television New Zealand (TVNZ) confirmed on Tuesday it would close five stations offering regional programming and launch a youth-oriented channel next month in their place.

The state-owned company also detailed plans to reposition its two core national channels, TV One and TV2, in a bid to clearly differentiate One for current affairs and sport and TV2 for entertainment-oriented content.
"The new channel is aimed at the 15-to-29-year-old market and will bring to New Zealanders some of the best music, fashion, movie and cult programming in the world," TVNZ said.
It did not name the new channel.

Rival company TV3, majority owned by Canada's CanWest Global Communications, already operates its TV3 channel nationally and within weeks will launch an entertainment-based stablemate to be called TV4.
TV4's launch is due three days before TVNZ's new youth network will take to the air on July 2.

The closure of TVNZ's five regional stations, grouped under the Horizon Pacific Television (HPTV) label, was announced on Monday when the company explained its plans to staff and confirmed details to news media.
HPTV has been widely reported to be losing about a million New Zealand dollars (US$700,000) a month.
TVNZ chief executive Chris Anderson told a news conference the moves were intended to make the group "stronger, more competitive and more relevant to its market".
He told national radio news that although the number of job losses had not yet been defined, about 100 redundancies were likely among HPTV staff.
Although it has a background as a state public broadcaster, TVNZ is now run as a commercial entity and all its stations carry advertising.
In its statement TVNZ said it planned to examine how the HPTV stations in Auckland, Hamilton, Wellington, Christchurch and Dunedin "can be offered for sale back to local interests".
Television division general manager Neil Roberts said the disposal might present a good opportunity for local radio and newspapers to join forces, but gave no further details.

Anderson said the group would be trying to reposition its core channels in the market place with an emphasis on locally-produced content, partly bringing in shows seen on HPTV. "We plan to strengthen our core brands, TV One and TV2, with as much quality New Zealand television as possible. At the same time we want to reach a young target market that has been somewhat neglected in the past," he said.

Critics of current broadcasting trends in New Zealand say the commercial rivalry between TVNZ and TV3 is bringing too much glitzy, commercially-packaged television onto the air comprised mainly of North American-sourced comedy and action dramas.
The main opposition Labour Party said in a statement the combination of a youth-oriented relaunch of HPTV and TV4 would not help meet the needs of the nation's television viewers.

"New Zealand has a diverse viewing audience and programming ought to reflect this. Only a fully-funded public broadcasting network would provide the variety of programmes demanded by differing sections of the viewing population," it said.
